episode_title: [ScaleX Bite-Size] - How to Bring Company Values to Life with Ron Lovett

real_qa.q: How does Ron Lovett gamify company values in his organizations?
real_qa.r: Ron Lovett gamifies values by pushing out one value every two weeks and rewarding employees with ballot entries for taking photos with the value card or writing it out. Additional ballots are earned for including coworkers, and prizes are drawn every two weeks. When collective participation hits 300 ballots, more significant prizes are awarded. This approach replaced command-and-control directives and allows values to create their own stories, connections, and fun among employees rather than top-down mandates from the C-suite.

real_qa.q: Why did Ron Lovett shift from using the word 'theme' to 'contest' in his values gamification program?
real_qa.r: Ron Lovett stopped using the word 'theme' because not everybody understands that terminology. He switched to calling it a 'contest' instead, though the two are essentially the same thing—it was simply a change of language to make the concept more accessible and understandable to all employees.
real_qa.requete: Ron Lovett theme contest values language

real_qa.q: How has Ron Lovett extended gamification beyond employees to customers at Beta?
real_qa.r: In his new business Beta, Ron Lovett has taken gamification to a new level by applying it to customers through community contests, not just employees. While many businesses have customer contests, he uses them strategically to drive business outcomes and push engagement out to the customer base, making gamification a tool he believes is significantly underutilized across organizations.
real_qa.requete: Ron Lovett Beta customer community contests gamification

real_qa.q: What was the financial crisis that prompted Ron Lovett's organizational turnaround?
real_qa.r: Ron Lovett's security and physical guarding company faced a million-dollar loss and he had to make a critical decision: close the business, do something else, or fundamentally change operations. He chose to implement a 24-month turnaround strategy centered on reshaping company culture and values engagement.
